Subject: Evidence request: partial redaction and signed hashes for admin activity

Hi Kimberly / Jordan,

As part of our SOC 2 readiness review we need a short-run export of admin activity covering the window 2026-10-01 -> 2026-11-01 for a scoped subset of users (Novamed tenant). The reviewer has asked for two specific things: 

- A manifest CSV listing admin actions (actor_id, action, object_type, timestamp, ip_decimal) with PII fields redacted where applicable, plus an attached SHA-256 checksum for the manifest file.
- A redaction exception form if any entries cannot be redacted due to forensic requirements.

Can you confirm that Redwood can produce the manifest in CSV, include a signed SHA-256 checksum, and provide a path for secure delivery (S3 presigned or SFTP)? Also need to understand the exact redaction rules you apply to email addresses and full names in the "actor" fields so the reviewer can evaluate sampling.

Thanks,
Aleksey Petrov
Security Lead, Novamed
security@novamed.com

Subject: Re: Evidence request: partial redaction and signed hashes for admin activity

Hi Aleksey — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce what you described. A few clarifications so we scope the export correctly: 

1) Scope: you requested tenant-level admin actions for Novamed. Do you want all admin roles or a subset (e.g., platform-admin + tenant-admin)?
2) Redaction: our standard export redacts user-visible PII for non-forensic exports. By default we hash email addresses and redact display_name except when an entry is required for investigation (that triggers a redaction exception).
3) Delivery: we can push to an S3 path (we'll provide a presigned URL valid 7 days) or deliver via secure SFTP. Which is preferred?
4) Manifest format: we'll include the CSV and a separate .sha256 file signed with our team key + the signed-attestation PDF.

I'll loop in Soojin (platform logs) for the exact field map and Ben (compliance) for the signed manifest process. If you need the unredacted dataset under an NDA, we can route that through our legal/custody process and capture an exception form.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

--
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 2) Redaction: our standard export redacts user-visible PII for non-forensic exports. By default we hash email addresses and redact display_name except when an entry is required for investigation (that triggers a redaction exception).

Hi all — technical details below to help the reviewer assess sampling and completeness. Short version: we can produce both redacted and exception (unredacted) outputs, with an attested manifest and sha256.

What we log (relevant fields): actor_id (internal UUID), actor_email (stored, may be hashed in export), actor_display_name, action_type, action_target_type, action_target_id, request_timestamp (RFC3339 UTC), request_remote_ip, request_user_agent, session_id, service_node, and request_payload_snippet (first 512 chars).

Redaction rules for exported manifests (default non-forensic):
- actor_email: SHA-256 hex of the lowercase email (salted with tenant id)
- actor_display_name: replaced with "REDACTED" unless included in exception list
- request_remote_ip: preserved but CIDR-truncated to /24 for privacy unless exception approved

Exception handling:
- If Novamed requires unredacted entries for specific investigations, they must sign the attached redaction-exception form. The form collects justification, account owner signoff, and retention window for the unredacted export. Requests without signed exception forms will be redacted and sampled.

Export packaging:
- CSV manifest (UTF-8, LF) named admin_audit_manifest_YYYYMMDD.csv
- accompanying admin_audit_manifest_YYYYMMDD.sha256 (hex digest)
- signed_attestation.pdf (signed by Redwood compliance lead)
- chain_of_custody.jsonl (we can provide an NDJSON trace of export actions if requested)

Delivery options: presigned S3 (7-day), SFTP with on-prem key exchange, or encrypted transfer via our partner secure-hub. Delivery will include checksums and a time-stamped signed attestation.

Sampling and verification: we can provide a deterministic sample mapping (rows 1..N) plus the salted-hash algorithm so the auditor can verify that the redaction was applied consistently.

I'll prepare the manifest and sha256 and tag Kimberly for the attestation signature.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

Hi Aleksey / Claire — following up with the deliverables and next steps. Per our internal checklist we completed the export for the Novamed tenant for 2026-10-01 -> 2026-11-01. Files staged:

- admin_audit_manifest_20261115.csv (4.2 MB)
- admin_audit_manifest_20261115.sha256 (contains hex digest)
- signed_attestation_20261115.pdf (compliance signature)
- redaction-exception-form-Novamed.pdf (empty unless you request unredacted rows)

Delivery: presigned S3 path provisioned (s3://redwood-evidence/novamed/2026-11-15/admin_manifest/) — we'll send the presigned URLs in a separate secure note. The SHA-256 digest is based on the CSV bytes (LF, UTF-8); we used our team key to sign the attestation PDF.

Verification guidance for auditors:
- We included a small verification script (documentation link in the Drive file) showing how to recompute the salted email hash (salt = tenant id) and compare against the manifest.
- If the auditor requires row-level unredaction for specific timestamps, please return a completed redaction-exception-form with legal signoff and retention instructions. We'll only produce unredacted exports upon receipt of that form and a short-term cross-team custody plan.

Let us know preferred delivery method (we'll proceed with the presigned S3 by default).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
